title: Decode One Instruction: 48 63 41 08
blurb: Challenge: Decode this x86-64 instruction byte by byte and state what it does: 48 63 41 08 (Windows x64 target). Answer: movsxd rax, dword ptr [rcx+8]. 48 = REX.W prefix (64-bit operand size). 63 = MOVSXD opcode (32-to-64-bit sign-extending move). 41 = ModRM byte 01 000 001: mod=01 (reg+disp8 addressing), reg=000 (dest=rax), rm=001 (base=rcx). 08 = disp8 offset +8. It reads the signed 32-bit dword at [rcx+8], sign-extends it to 64 bits, and stores it in rax -- the classic pattern for loading a signed int field (e.g. an index or count) from a struct pointed to by rcx, the first-argument register in the Windows x64 calling convention, while widening it for pointer arithmetic.
